reason: E3 supports that laser cladding can produce well-bonded, homogeneous coatings on TC4, and E2 shows a BCC-phase RHEA coating on steel can greatly improve hardness and wear resistance at room and elevated temperatures. However, no cited evidence addresses the functionally graded design, the specific TiZrAlNbCo system, or the formation of a BCC matrix with minor Laves phases, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Laser cladding can produce homogeneous, dense, well-bonded coatings on TC4
Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) can provide high hardness and wear resistance
A functionally graded design can minimize thermal/microstructural mismatch and promote strong adhesion
A BCC-phase RHEA with minor secondary phases offers dispersion strengthening and reduces residual stress
The proposed TiZrAlNbCo RHEA system will form the desired BCC + minor Laves phase microstructure
